dedupe_keys.name: suez canal bosporus strait and bab el mandeb strait transits during disruptions ais derived adb

description: This dataset from the Asian Development Bank gives daily and monthly counts of ship transits through three maritime chokepoints during disruptions: the Suez Canal during the 2021 blockage, the Bosporus Strait after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait during the Houthi attacks on shipping. Counts are derived from Automatic Identification System (AIS) ship signals with the framework of the paper "Analyzing anomalous events in passageways with high-frequency ship signals" (PLOS ONE, 2025), and the files add monthly net tonnage, transits by ship type, official Suez Canal Authority counts and estimates from Lloyd's List Intelligence for validation, plus rerouting maps. Coverage runs from January 2019 to March 2024. The CSV and HTML files are free on the Humanitarian Data Exchange under CC BY, and the code to reproduce them is on ADB's GitHub. Caveats: it covers three passages and the period of the study only, with no update schedule; AIS coverage and the transit detection method shape the counts; and some validation series come from a commercial provider. The data support resilience and network flow studies of maritime chokepoint closures and rerouting, such as calibrating disruption scenarios for shipping networks; related records are IMF PortWatch and the World Bank global shipping traffic density.
name: Suez Canal, Bosporus Strait and Bab el-Mandeb Strait transits during disruptions (AIS-derived, ADB)

sources.note: ADB; CC BY; 2019-01-01 to 2024-03-31; daily transits for Suez blockage, Bosporus (Ukraine invasion), Bab el-Mandeb (Houthi attacks); AIS-based; official, Lloyd's List and own estimates; code on GitHub; modified 2025-07-15

title_en: Suez Canal, Bosporus Strait and Bab el-Mandeb Strait transits during disruptions (AIS-derived, ADB)
